keyPoints: A queue removes values in the same order they were inserted.

The example rejects a full insertion without changing existing values.

slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 6, treat 6.1.1 Enqueuing and Dequeuing Values as an algorithmic claim. Enqueue adds a value after all currently queued values. Dequeue returns the oldest remaining value or reports an empty queue. The optional result distinguishes an empty queue from a legitimate stored zero. For the ring queue, the invariant is 0 <= size <= capacity, with head identifying the oldest occupied logical position when size is positive. A full insertion returns false before any slot is modified. This lets the caller decide whether to retry, apply backpressure, or record a dropped sample; the container does not silently make that operational decision.
